description: 30 original algorithmic problems, medium difficulty. Each problem ships hidden test cases used for programmatic scoring (no LLM judge).

items.prompt: Return the length of the longest contiguous subarray whose elements are strictly increasing.
Given a string, return the longest substring containing at most 2 distinct characters.
Return all integers from 1 to n (inclusive) that are NOT divisible by any prime greater than 5. Order ascending.
Given a 2D grid of 0s and 1s, return the number of connected groups of 1s (4-directional connectivity).

items.signature: def solve(nums: list[int], k: int) -> int
items.prompt: Return the number of subarrays whose sum equals k.
Merge overlapping intervals. Each interval is [start, end] inclusive. Return merged intervals sorted by start.

items.signature: def solve(s: str, t: str) -> bool
items.prompt: Return True iff s and t are anagrams (same multiset of characters).
Given a non-empty list, return the element that appears more than n/2 times. Guaranteed to exist.
Given a string of parens '(', ')', '{', '}', '[', ']', return the length of the longest valid (well-formed) substring.
Given daily stock prices, return max profit from at most 2 buy-sell transactions. You must sell before buying again.

items.signature: def solve(nums: list[int], target: int) -> list[int]
items.prompt: Find two distinct indices i, j such that nums[i] + nums[j] == target. Return [i, j] with i < j. Guaranteed exactly one solution.
Return elements of a matrix in spiral order (right, down, left, up, repeat).
Return the number of distinct ways to climb a staircase of n steps, taking 1 or 2 steps at a time.
Reverse the words in a sentence. Words are separated by single spaces. Leading/trailing whitespace and multiple spaces should be collapsed.
Return all unique triplets [a,b,c] in nums such that a+b+c == 0. No duplicate triplets. Order within triplet ascending; outer order doesn't matter (will be normalized).
Given a string of digits, decode it as A=1..Z=26. Return number of valid decodings. '0' alone is invalid.
Given meeting intervals [start, end], return min number of rooms required so no two meetings in the same room overlap.
Return product of all elements except self, without using division. Order preserved.

items.signature: def solve(s: str, p: str) -> bool
items.prompt: Implement simple wildcard match: '?' matches any single char, '*' matches any sequence (including empty). Return True iff p fully matches s.
Return the missing positive integer (smallest positive int not in nums). nums may contain duplicates/negatives.
Group anagrams. Return groups; order of groups and within-group order doesn't matter (will be normalized by sorting).
Return all valid combinations of n pairs of parentheses, sorted lexicographically.
Minimum path sum from top-left to bottom-right of grid, moving only right or down.

items.signature: def solve(s: str, k: int) -> int
items.prompt: Length of longest substring with at most k distinct characters.

items.signature: def solve(coins: list[int], amount: int) -> int
items.prompt: Minimum number of coins to make `amount`. Return -1 if impossible. Unlimited supply of each coin denomination.
Return True iff s is a palindrome considering only alphanumeric characters, case-insensitive.

input: A man, a plan, a canal: Panama

items.prompt: Find the contiguous subarray with the largest sum and return that sum. Array has at least one element.

items.signature: def solve(s: str, words: list[str]) -> bool
items.prompt: Return True iff s can be segmented into a sequence of one or more words from the given list (words may be reused).
Given an array where every element appears twice except one, find the single one. Linear time, O(1) extra space.

items.signature: def solve(n: int, edges: list[list[int]]) -> bool
items.prompt: Given n nodes (0..n-1) and undirected edges, return True iff the graph is a valid tree (connected, no cycles).
